title: Stability sprint handoff snapshot — Feb 14 2028
content:
Summary:

Quick handoff note for the week ending Feb 14, 2028. Focused on three incident clusters (edge cache regressions, failing KV eviction under tail latency, and two brief region network flaps), an SLO deviation window on embeddings route, and one service-level deployment rollback. This doc contains the standup notes, incident synopses, current SLO snapshot, items we handed to next on-call, and a short list of runway actions for next sprint.

Context and tone:
- This is an informal working doc for on-call handoffs — expect bullets, unfinished TODOs, and pointers to JIRA/PRs.
- If you are picking up the next shift, start with the open owners table below and check the pinned Slack thread in #sre-ops.

What happened this week (high level):
1) Edge cache regressions (Feb 11–12) — intermittent 5–10% 95th token latency regressions for hosted API in us-west-2 during peak batches.
   - Impact: customer-visible elevated tail latency for generation endpoints; no data loss.
   - Root cause (current hypothesis): a recently merged micro-optimization in the serving-runtime batching path (PR #1782) changed the batching window heuristics for short-window requests, causing smaller-than-expected batches and increased per-token overhead under certain request distributions.
   - Mitigation: reverted the change 2028-02-12 03:12 UTC; applied temporary conservative batching config.
   - Next steps: create controlled A/B test for alternative heuristics, add synthetic workload test for short-window distributions. Follow-up ticket: SRE-4123.

2) KV cache eviction thrash under tail traffic (Feb 13) — observed elevated cpu and GPU mem churn on dedicated hosts serving long-context chat sessions.
   - Impact: transient model stalls resulting in request timeouts (0.4% of requests) and degraded throughput on a handful of dedicated pools.
   - Findings: eviction logic triggered too aggressively when a small percentage of sessions sent bursty long sequences; combined with an aging policy that preferred freeing large KV chunks first, causing recompute thrash.
   - Mitigation: tuned eviction thresholds and changed priority to LRU across sequence-length, added a short grace period for active sessions. Changes rolled to staging and then prod on 2028-02-14 11:00 UTC.
   - Owner for follow-up: Miguel Alvarez (ticket SRE-4198).

3) Regional network flaps (Feb 10, Feb 14) — two brief periods of degraded connectivity between our private control plane and a cloud region (ap-southeast-1).
   - Impact: control-plane API latencies spiked, briefly affecting Private deployment control operations (no model inference impact for existing pinned nodes).
   - Mitigation: route failover to secondary control-plane endpoint, escalated to cloud provider; provider reported transient routing instability.
   - Action: add control-plane multi-homing checklist to runbook. Owner: Omar Hassan.

4) Deployment rollback (Feb 12) — a versioned runtime rollout to dedicated pools hit a compatibility mismatch with an older quantization profile used by a small customer cohort.
   - Impact: one customer reported degraded output quality; rollout was paused and rolled back.
   - Action: add a guard in rollout tooling to detect mismatched quant profiles before canary. Owner: Priya Singh.

Standup log (select items from daily standups):
- 2028-02-13 09:00 UTC — Leah: noted edge-cache tail increase; Omar tracing logs and flagged PR #1782. Miguel: investigating KV eviction. Priya: paused runway deployments where needed.
- 2028-02-13 17:00 UTC — Omar: rolling config change on batch window on canary; Leah: started incident postmortem draft.
- 2028-02-14 08:30 UTC — Miguel: staging tests show reduced thrash after eviction tuning; will promote tonight.
- 2028-02-14 12:00 UTC — Priya: rollout guard implemented in dev tooling; prepping small PR and test cases.

SLO snapshot (current, rolling 30d where applicable):
- Generation API (hosted) availability (success rate): 99.92% (target 99.95%) — small deficit driven by Feb 11–12 tail events.
- Generation API p95 latency: 420ms (target 400ms) — tail pressure on short-window batches.
- Embeddings API availability: 99.88% (target 99.99%) — a transient error spike from an upstream dependency on Feb 14; monitoring alert escalated.
- Dedicated cluster throughput SLA: within expected capacity; one pool had degraded ops during KV thrash window but recovered after tuning.

Immediate action items (timeboxed):
- [A1] Add short-window synthetic workload to CI perf bucket to catch batching regressions (owner: Leah, due: 2028-02-21).
- [A2] Implement A/B test harness for alternate batching heuristics and run for 48h (owner: Omar, due: 2028-02-25).
- [A3] Finish SRE-4198 eviction logic refactor and add unit+integration tests (owner: Miguel, due: 2028-02-20).
- [A4] Add rollout guard to deployment service to validate quant profiles before canary (owner: Priya, due: 2028-02-18).
- [A5] Draft runbook entry for control-plane multi-homing & test failover runbook (owner: Omar, due: 2028-02-28).

Hand-off table (open ownership at time of doc):
- SRE-4123 (batching regression) — Leah — in-progress — next: metrics dashboard for canary distribution.
- SRE-4198 (KV eviction) — Miguel — in-progress — next: deploy to 2 prod pools and monitor.
- Rollout guard PR — Priya — review queued, QA scheduled.
- Control-plane multi-homing runbook — Omar — draft started.

Notes to next on-call:
- If you see p95 jump but availability stable, check batch-size histogram first. Use the internal perf dashboard (link in JIRA SRE-4123) to correlate batch size vs p95.
- For persistent KV thrash, check: eviction counters, active session list, and recent long-context session ids (we log session-id in traces). Avoid aggressive eviction pushes until Miguel's refactor is live.
- For control-plane blips, failover should be automatic but sometimes the DNS TTL was not honored by older clients; have a manual failover checklist in /confluence/sre/handbook.

Open questions and risks:
- Do we need a separate perf SLO for short-window vs long-window workloads? Current SLOs aggregate across request distributions and hide distributional regressions. Proposal: create a p95_short_window SLO for hosted generation. (Discuss in SLO working group.)
- Can we simulate the exact customer long-chat burst pattern in staging? Current synthetic workloads approximate but don't cover multi-tenant collision patterns.
- Rollout tooling: how to enforce compatibility matrix for quant/arch combos without bloating the release process? (Priya to propose options.)

Follow-ups for the SLO working group:
- Leah to prepare a short proposal with histogram-backed SLO buckets (due: 2028-02-22).
- Miguel to present eviction refactor plan and regtest design in WG sync (2028-02-19).

Reference timeline for notable events:
- 2028-02-10 05:40 UTC — Regional control-plane flap (ap-southeast-1) — failover exercised.
- 2028-02-11 22:10 UTC — Edge cache tail latency increases detected.
- 2028-02-12 03:12 UTC — Reversion of batching micro-opt applied.
- 2028-02-12 15:00 UTC — Rollout paused and rolled back for quant profile mismatch.
- 2028-02-13 07:00 UTC — Begin investigation into KV eviction thrash.
- 2028-02-14 11:00 UTC — Eviction config promoted to prod pools.

Appendix / quick links:
- Incident tickets: SRE-4123, SRE-4198
- Perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1782
- Rollout guard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-service/pull/492 (WIP)
- Runbook (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/handbook+stability-sprint-2028-02

Raw observability pointers (for triage):
- Batch size distribution dashboard: /dashboards/ops/batch-size-vs-latency
- KV eviction counters: /metrics/kv/eviction_counter and /traces?filter=event:kv-eviction
- Control-plane endpoint health: /health/control-plane/multi-region

Closing notes (tone):
- Team did a good job catching the edge regression quickly and reverting to a safer config. The KV eviction thrash is the more subtle reliability risk — it's intermittent under tail patterns and needs both code-level fixes and better integration tests.
- If anything in the doc is stale by the time you pick this up, triage the owners listed above and move items to the weekly board.

— Leah

Quick checklist before the next shift:
- Verify SRE-4198 pipeline test run status.
- Confirm rollback guard merged or blocked PR reason.
- Ping cloud provider contact if any further control-plane blips appear.
- Post short note in #sre-ops summarizing changes promoted to prod.
